summary: High-margin subscription software compounder. The distortion to watch is stock-based compensation: it is a real cost to owners that GAAP operating cash flow adds back, so headline FCF flatters per-share economics while the share count is only held flat by large buybacks. Judge Intuit on SBC-adjusted free cash flow per share and on whether buybacks are actually shrinking the count.

metrics.label: SBC / revenue
metrics.why: Sizes the compensation cost that operating cash flow adds back. For software compounders this is the main gap between reported FCF and what actually accrues to existing shareholders.
metrics.evidence: FY2022 10-K: AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpenseNetOfTax $912M against revenue; SBC is among the largest non-cash add-backs in the cash-flow statement.

metrics.label: Buybacks / SBC (dilution offset)
metrics.why: Shows how much of the buyback is merely mopping up shares issued to employees rather than returning capital. Near 1x, repurchases are offsetting dilution, not compounding per-share value.
metrics.evidence: FY2022: TreasuryStockValueAcquiredCostMethod $1.9B against SBC of similar order.

annotations.fcf: Adds back stock-based compensation, a genuine cost to existing owners. Compare against Adj. FCF (FCF − SBC) rather than using this figure for per-share value.
annotations.gross_profit: Intuit stopped separately tagging cost of goods and cost of services after FY2017, so the split components are unavailable for later years; the consolidated gross profit line continues.

caveats: cost_of_goods_component and cost_of_services_component are tagged only 2009-2017; the app already derives consolidated cost of revenue, but the product-versus-service split is not available after that.
Advertising expense runs ~$1.6B (FY2022) and is a major discretionary lever on reported margin; it is disclosed but not currently tracked as a metric.
treasury_stock_shares is tagged only 2010-2013, so cumulative buyback share counts are incomplete.
